page: Microsoft Azure E16ps_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by the ARM64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, configured with 1 thread per core. The instance is paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware caches include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. There are no onboard GPUs and no bundled local storage disks, requiring remote network storage for persistent or temporary files.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier throughput across multi-threaded and memory-bound operations. The instance achieved 28,894.58 on stress-ng multi-core testing, a PassMark CPU score of 11,570.19, and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 9,647.0. Large-block memory bandwidth delivers 127.65 GB/sec for reads and 67.48 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, the server registers 22.74 million Redis SET operations per second and 19.04 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff lies in single-threaded performance and legacy instruction support. The Geekbench single-core score of 1,116.0, PassMark encryption score of 2,606.46, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression of 8.81 GB/sec fall into the lower quartile. The processor also lacks x86-specific vector or matrix extensions like AVX-512 and AMX, and prompt processing for small and medium LLM models shows lower throughput (19.08 tokens/sec on 7B models).

Because of its high 8 GB per vCPU resource density and predictable single-threaded core isolation, Azure E16ps_v5 is architecturally well suited for memory-intensive workloads that scale horizontally across cores. Primary workload fits include in-memory databases like Redis, mid-sized relational database management systems, data caching layers, and web application serving tiers that do not rely on local high-speed disk storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E16ps_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated ARM64 vCPUs on an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, coupled with 128.0 GB of RAM. Operating without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core), the instance yields an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It contains no onboard GPUs and provides no local storage, relying on attached storage volumes. Multi-threaded benchmark testing reflects solid middle-tier performance, highlighted by 22.74 million Redis SET operations per second, a multi-core Geekbench score of 9,647.0, and 127.65 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. Conversely, single-thread metrics and instruction sets without x86 vector extensions represent measurable performance tradeoffs. Given its dedicated core layout and dense memory allocation, the E16ps_v5 fits in-memory caching systems, distributed databases, and general memory-intensive applications.
